title: bug: no runner ever reattaches, so a daemon restart releases every live seat's row once the reconcile window passes
description:
CONTRACT DRIFT between Wave 1 slices. Filed by the governor on 2026-09-17 after verifying it in source; no live incident on a live seat yet.

THE DAEMON HALF SHIPPED
- task-58f7db9a: a restart parks running attempts in `reconciling`.
- task-d7fa98f4: runReconcileWindowSweep gives up on an attempt that stays `reconciling` longer than reconcileWindowMs (2h by default, counted from lastPhaseAt). It then unassigns a row that is still assigned to that attempt's owner. There is deliberately no liveness check.
- task-06b658be: moe.heartbeat answers `reattachRequired: true, reattachWith: 'moe.reattach_attempt'` for a reconciling attempt (src/tools/heartbeat.ts:46-62, 103).
- moe.reattach_attempt returns the attempt to `running` only when the caller's processStartedAt and host match what the attempt recorded.

THE RUNNER HALF WAS NEVER BUILT
1. A real claim records no process identity. openClaimAttempt passes only taskId, workerId, runnerId=workerId and workspace, and its comment says "A distinct runner identity and a per-attempt workspace arrive with the reattachment work" (src/tools/claimNextTask.ts:69-76). claim_next_task takes no processStartedAt or host.
2. Reattach therefore never matches a production attempt: src/tools/reattachAttempt.ts:109 refuses one with 'processStartedAt (none recorded)'.
3. Neither launcher calls it: `grep -i reattach scripts/moe-agent.ps1 scripts/moe-agent.sh` finds nothing. The heartbeat sidecar ignores reattachRequired.
4. Wave 1 acceptance case 4 ("restarting only the daemon during a long build preserves ownership") passes only because its fixture writes processStartedAt and host straight into the attempt record and then plays the runner itself (src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts:1690-1718).

CONSEQUENCE IN THE REAL FLEET
After any daemon restart:
- Every live seat's attempt is parked.
- Once the window passes, the sweep unassigns the row out from under that still-running seat.
Until task-c628902e is built, that seat keeps calling start_step and complete_step on the now-unassigned row without any refusal (the assertWorkerOwns early return). Meanwhile a second worker can claim the same row, so two seats do the same work. After c628902e, the seat gets TASK_NOT_CLAIMED and must re-claim under a new generation.
Related evidence:
- task-49ec8755's QA reject, issue 2, measured the wrapper side: a `reconciling` attempt stops the loop, and "the wrappers never reattach".
- 2026-09-17: dead worker-a7127038's row was released through exactly this sweep path at 16:53:38Z. That was correct for a dead seat, and a live seat is treated the same way.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW
Activating task-2a7e0f5b's fix needs a daemon rebuild and restart, and the restart window is the human's call. Every restart from now on is subject to this gap.

DIRECTION (the architect decides, probably via a SPIDR split; it spans the daemon, both launchers and the harnesses)
- Claims opened by a runner record that runner's process identity.
- The runner (the wrapper, which outlives CLI respawns) reacts to the heartbeat's reattachRequired by calling moe.reattach_attempt with that identity before the window expires.
- The give-up half stays as it is for seats that really are dead.
definitionOfDone: An attempt opened by a wrapper-launched claim records the runner's processStartedAt and host, and moe.reattach_attempt accepts that identity after a daemon-only restart (daemon test with a real restart, not a fixture-seeded attempt record).

Both wrappers reattach: after a daemon-only restart, a live seat whose heartbeat answers reattachRequired calls moe.reattach_attempt, the attempt returns to running, and the reconcile-window sweep no longer releases that row. Proven in the launcher harness for sh and ps1; parity-check passes.
A different process (mismatched processStartedAt or host) still cannot reattach, and a seat that never reattaches is still given up after reconcileWindowMs exactly as task-d7fa98f4 shipped.

docs/MCP_SERVER.md (claim_next_task, heartbeat, reattach_attempt) and the restart story in CLAUDE.md/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md describe the runner reattach path as shipped; daemon npm test and npx tsc --noEmit pass.
taskRails: The daemon stays state-only; process identity is supplied by the runner, never probed by the daemon.
Do not add any idle-based release of WORKING/PLANNING tasks, and do not weaken the give-up for seats that never reattach.
Both launchers or neither: moe-agent.ps1 and moe-agent.sh change together.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 4a — capture the identity and send it at claim time, in both twins.

- Compute the pair once, at wrapper start, into MOE_PROCESS_STARTED_AT and MOE_HOST (sh) and $script:MoeProcessStartedAt / $script:MoeHost (ps1), with the spellings fixed in step 1. Log them once at pre-flight, at the same verbosity as the other one-line pre-flight facts.
- Add both to every claim_next_task call the wrapper makes, including the resume path. They are optional daemon-side, so an older daemon ignores them and nothing breaks.
- Do NOT send them on any other tool call: they are the claim's record of which process opened the attempt, not a general header.

Error handling: if either value cannot be determined (an unreadable /proc, a Get-Process failure, an empty hostname), send NEITHER, log one `[WARN]` naming what failed, and continue. A partial identity is worse than none: it records something no later reattach can reproduce, and a claim must never fail because of it.

Arm `identity-claim` from step 2 turns green.
implementationPlan.note:
The identity is captured once and sent on every claim, in both twins.

sh (moe_runner_identity, defined and called once, top-level, right after proc_start_token):
- Token is "$$@$(proc_start_token $$)". Where /proc is absent (macOS) it falls back to ps lstart with whitespace squeezed.
- Host is live_marker_host. These are the SAME helpers the live-session marker already uses (ponytail rung 2: no second probe of "which process on which host").
- Validation matches the daemon's: non-empty, no [[:cntrl:]], at most 200/255.
- Results go to MOE_PROCESS_STARTED_AT and MOE_HOST (shell variables, not exported) and CLAIM_RPC_JSON (CLAIM_JSON plus the pair, built by json.dumps).
- Both claim_next_task RPCs (pre-flight, taskless-wait retry) use CLAIM_RPC_JSON. That covers the resume path too: the resume is the same claim call.

ps1 (the same block right after Get-MoeProcStartToken):
- Token is "$PID@$(Get-MoeProcStartToken $PID)" (StartTime UTC ticks). Host is Get-MoeLiveMarkerHost.
- A [char]::IsControl scan and length bounds are applied.
- Results go to $script:MoeProcessStartedAt, $script:MoeHost and $claimRpcArgs (the claim object plus the two NoteProperties). Both claim_next_task RPCs use $claimRpcArgs.

One pre-flight line, printed once at start: "Runner identity: processStartedAt=<v> host=<h>".
- If either value cannot be read, NEITHER is sent and one "[WARN] Runner identity unavailable (<why>); claims carry no processStartedAt/host, so this seat cannot reattach after a daemon restart." is logged.
- The claim itself is never failed for this.

Not sent on any other call:
- The prompts' CLAIM_JSON / $claimJson (the text the CLI sees) is unchanged.
- reattach_attempt carries the pair because that tool requires it.

Evidence:
- identity-claim is green on sh, pwsh and 5.1. The general 'every claim carries the runner identity' check passes on all 8 arms.
- Real daemon plus real proxy (scratch e2e, see the step-6 note): the attempt the claim opened records exactly the pair the wrapper printed.
  - sh: 737300@73504691 / yaron-pc.
  - pwsh: 56680@639253420725444419 / yaron-pc.
  - 5.1: 59468@639253420858687705 / yaron-pc.
- Measured: a bash exec hot-reload keeps the same pid and start token, so the identity is stable across it. A ps1 self-restart is a new process with a new identity, which is correct: it deregisters first.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 4b — react to reattachRequired, in both twins. This is the half that keeps a live seat's row after a daemon restart.

(a) The heartbeat sidecar stops discarding the reply. Pass it the pinned identity at start (taskId, attemptId, generation, processStartedAt, host alongside the workerId it already gets), then on each ping parse the answer:
- `reattachRequired` with reason `attempt-reconciling` AND an attemptId equal to the pinned one → send moe.reattach_attempt with taskId, workerId, runnerId, attemptId, generation, processStartedAt and host. The heartbeat carries no generation, which is exactly why the sidecar holds the pinned one.
- Any other reason, or an attemptId that is not this seat's → do nothing but log once. There is nothing this process may reattach.
- A refusal → log once and STOP attempting for that attempt id. ATTEMPT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH never heals, and a per-ping retry would spam the daemon every 60 s for hours.
- A successful reattach → log once and go back to plain pings.

(b) The main loop reattaches too, for the window the sidecar cannot cover: when the wrapper reads its own pinned attempt record and finds phase `reconciling` — at pre-flight before launching the CLI, and after the CLI exits before the landing path — send the same call first. Without it, a restart during a CLI run leaves record_candidate and the finalize ladder failing closed on a reconciling attempt and the bytes parked for no reason.

(c) Error handling, and it decides whether this is safe to ship: the sidecar is best-effort and must never throw, never exit its loop early, and never fail the session. Every parse and every RPC is wrapped; an unparseable reply is ignored; a transport failure is one log line and the next tick tries again. The main-loop reattach is the same: a failure logs one `[WARN]` and the landing proceeds exactly as it does today, because a reattach that could not be sent is not a reason to lose bytes.

Arms `reattach-sidecar`, `reattach-refused`, `reattach-postflight` and `reattach-none` from step 2 turn green.
implementationPlan.note:
Both twins now react to reattachRequired.

(a) SIDECAR
- sh: the start_heartbeat_sidecar subshell inherits the pinned MOE_ATTEMPT_ID, MOE_ATTEMPT_GENERATION, PREFLIGHT_TASK_ID, MOE_RUNNER_ID and the identity at fork.
- ps1: Start-HeartbeatSidecar passes a $pin hashtable to the job through -ArgumentList. The job cannot see script variables.
- Each ping now reads the reply:
  - attempt-reconciling naming the pinned attempt id, with an identity present: send moe.reattach_attempt with the pinned generation (the answer carries none), then log one line.
  - Any other reason or attempt id: log once per reason per sidecar ('... pinned no such reconciling attempt; nothing to reattach.').
  - A refusal (a daemon error carrying a codeName): log once and set refused, so that attempt is never asked again in this sidecar.
  - No usable answer: '[WARN] ... retrying later.', and the next ping tries again.
- sh pre-checks the reply for 'reattachRequired' before spending a python parse, so a plain {ok:true} costs nothing extra.
- ps1 prints the job's lines in Stop-HeartbeatSidecar from ChildJobs.Output. Receive-Job throws 'The Persistence Path does not exist' on 5.1 when the profile path is absent, which is exactly the harness's fake USERPROFILE. Found by the 5.1 arm run. Memory: gotcha-ps51-receive-job-persistence-path.

(b) MAIN LOOP
- reattach_own_attempts / Invoke-MoeReattachOwnAttempts reattach every attempt THIS worker owns in `reconciling` (read from .moe/attempts).
- Where it runs:
  - right after the pre-flight claim, BEFORE pin_attempt_identity / Set-MoeAttemptIdentity (a resume after a restart would otherwise fail the pin closed);
  - right after the CLI exits, before status resolution and the landing.
- Its refusals are remembered for the life of the wrapper process.
- Deviation, argued: I scan the seat's own reconciling attempts on disk rather than only the pinned id. That covers a resume, where nothing is pinned yet, and BLOCKED holds. The daemon's identity check still decides who may reattach.
- Shared RPC helper: moe_reattach / Invoke-MoeReattach. Returns 0/'running', 1/'refused', 2/'none'.

(c) SAFETY
- The sh sidecar runs under set +e. Every RPC and parse is `|| continue`, so a failure costs one tick and the loop never exits early.
- The ps1 job body is try/catch per tick.
- The main-loop calls are `|| true`, and the helpers never return non-zero to the caller under set -e. An RPC failure logs one WARN and the landing proceeds unchanged.

Evidence:
- sh: 5/5 reattach arms green, plus identity-claim and the two reconciling arms.
- pwsh and PowerShell 5.1: 8/8 each.
- REAL daemon + real proxy + new wrapper, abrupt daemon-only restart mid-CLI (scratch e2e):
  - sh, pwsh and 5.1 each saw attempt -> reconciling -> running within 2-3 s via the sidecar, same generation, task still assigned (WORKING).
  - The wrapper logged '[reattach] attempt <id> (generation 1) on task task-e2e is running again after a daemon restart.'

Parity registrations, the restart story, and the MCP docs are updated.

comments.author: worker-d0c3b06e
comments.content:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW (step 7), worker-d0c3b06e. Diff: 8 files, +493/-36. The scripts are byte-identical to the snapshot every suite ran against.

1. IDENTITY STABILITY
- Computed once, at wrapper start, then cached:
  - sh: moe_runner_identity is called once at top level. The value goes into MOE_PROCESS_STARTED_AT/MOE_HOST and is folded into CLAIM_RPC_JSON.
  - ps1: a top-level block fills $script:MoeProcessStartedAt/$script:MoeHost and $claimRpcArgs.
- Every claim, the sidecar $pin and the main-loop reattach reuse those cached values. Nothing recomputes them, so a later hostname change cannot desynchronise them.
- Proof: identity-claim (loop, >=2 claims, one pair). A general check on all 64 frozen modes: every claim carries one pair.
- Wrapper respawn: a new process means a new pid and start token. Its reattach of the old attempt is refused with ATTEMPT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH, logged once and remembered. The row is given up after reconcileWindowMs. That is correct: that execution is gone.
- Caveat: a resume ADOPTS the opener's recorded identity. A wrapper that resumed a predecessor's attempt cannot reattach it after a later restart. That is the daemon's rule; I left it alone.
- CORRECTION to my step-3 note: on Git Bash (MSYS), bash `exec` keeps the pid but CHANGES the /proc starttime (measured: 741284@73624917 -> 741284@73624973). On Linux both survive. It is harmless: the hot-reload exec path deregisters before exec, so no attempt stays pinned to the old identity.

2. GIVE-UP UNCHANGED
- No daemon file touched. npm test is identical to the baseline (122 files, 2105 passed | 1 skipped), and it includes bd799955's give-up tests (checkReconcileWindow closes the attempt and releases the row).
- The wrappers add exactly one daemon call, reattach_attempt, which moves a matching reconciling attempt back to running.
- There is no release_task, no idle signal and no lastActivityAt read anywhere in the added lines (grep of the + lines). Task rail 2 holds.

3. STRANGER
- Daemon: refuses before any write with -32002 ATTEMPT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH. Seen live in my real-daemon e2e: processStartedAt '1@1' refused on sh, pwsh and 5.1.
- Wrapper, sidecar: any daemon error carrying a codeName sets `refused`, logs once, and is never asked again that session.
- Wrapper, main loop: remembers the attempt id for the wrapper's life.
- Covered by reattach-refused (1 row across 3+ later pings) and the M3/pm3 mutants (a forgotten refusal reddens it).

4. SIDECAR SAFETY (separate process: sh subshell / ps1 Start-Job; its status is ignored)
- Unparseable reply: sh `python ... || continue`; ps1 ConvertFrom-Json inside a per-tick try/catch.
- Dead transport: sh `moe_rpc ... || continue`. ps1 Send-SidecarRpc returns $null, so there is no ask. A dead reattach call is 'none', gets one WARN, and the next ping retries.
- Daemon restarted mid-ping: the ping fails or reaches the new daemon. Proven by the e2e: abrupt kill mid-CLI, then reconciling -> running within ~3 s.
- Refusal: see 3.
- Wrapper already exited: `kill -0` / Get-Process break (unchanged). Every stop path is unchanged.
- ps1 5.1: Receive-Job throws under a missing profile path, so lines are read from ChildJobs.Output inside a try.
- The sidecar cannot fail the session. The main-loop calls are `|| true` and never return non-zero under set -e.

5. TIMING
- 60 s pings against a 2 h window is about 120 chances.
- If MOE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SEC is raised past 7200, or MOE_HEARTBEAT_MAX_DURATION_SEC ends early, or MOE_DISABLE_HEARTBEAT=1: the sweep can give the attempt up before the next ping. The ping then answers no-open-attempt or no-worker-record (logged once), and the row is released.
- The only remaining cover is the main loop, at the next claim or CLI exit.
- NOTHING warns. It is not clamped, per the plan.

6. MAIN-LOOP REATTACH
- The case: a restart between sessions, or inside a session that ended before the next ping, leaves the attempt reconciling at the next pre-flight.
- Without the reattach: moe_attempt_read accepts only running|finalizing, so the resume pin fails. The completion's candidate evidence is then 'unavailable', the bytes go to a rescue ref, and finalize is refused. The loop stops.
- Arms: reattach-preflight (pre-flight site). reattach-postflight, checkpoint-reconciling and manual-reconciling (post-flight site).
- M2 (sidecar-only mutant) reddens all four.

7. TWINS
- Same rules. Identity: pid@start-token + lowercased host, both-or-neither. Sidecar: pinned id + pinned generation. Other reasons: noted once. Refusal: stop. None: retry. Main loop: own reconciling attempts on disk, right after the claim and after the CLI, refusals remembered.
- Only mechanics differ (subshell vs Start-Job).
- Parity PASS on sh, pwsh and 5.1. The guard is proven: a reworded literal in one twin fails all three.
- The harness shared regions are byte-identical, and the same 8 arms are green on sh, pwsh and 5.1.

8. EMBARRASSMENT
- Worst case 1: the fleet daemon (started 2026-09-17T20:00Z) predates bd799955. Nothing is recorded or reattachable until a human rebuilds and restarts it.
  - The wrappers are compatible: I probed the old dist, and a claim with the pair succeeds with the pair ignored.
  - This must be said to whoever schedules the restart.
- Worst case 2: repo-launched ps1 seats hot-reload this wrapper as soon as it is on disk.
  - Mitigations: parse 0 errors on both engines; full ps1 suites green on both (64/28); a real-daemon e2e green on both.
- Worst case 3: a seat whose attempt a respawned wrapper resumed cannot reattach, so its row is released after 2 h (pre-existing class).
  - reattach-refused covers that the wrapper stays sane. The release itself is daemon-side and unchanged.

Scratch: all trees are deleted; none had junctions (verified, 0 reparse points). Kept for QA: D:/moe-t5e09-e2e/e2e.mjs (real daemon + proxy + wrapper restart run: `node e2e.mjs sh|ps1|ps51`), old-daemon.mjs, and the full sh log.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
The card asked for a SPIDR split and the human chose it: the daemon half is now task-bd799955 (claim_next_task records the identity; ~3 files) and this card is the runner half. Whole, it was about 10 files — the plan-size ceiling — with no room for a surprise.

- The heartbeat sidecar is the actor, because it is the only part of the wrapper that is alive while the CLI blocks the main loop for the whole session. It already pings every 60 s against a 2 h reconcile window, so the margin is enormous.
- The main loop reattaches too, but only where it reads its own pinned attempt and finds it reconciling. Without that, a restart during a CLI run leaves record_candidate and the finalize ladder failing closed and parks bytes for no reason.
- Identity is `<pid>@<process start token>` plus host, computed once. pid alone is not enough (reuse), the start token alone is not enough (shared ticks), and a recomputed value would refuse every reattach — the daemon compares exact strings.
- Rejected: having the daemon derive or probe the identity (task rail 1, and the daemon never touches processes). Rejected: reattaching from a respawned wrapper — that is a different process and must not adopt the old execution. Rejected: retrying a refused reattach on every ping — ATTEMPT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH never heals and the retry would spam the daemon for hours. Rejected: touching docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, which task-808869c5's docs sweep currently owns.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- attemptStore.openAttempt already persists processStartedAt and host when supplied; only claim_next_task never offered them (the prerequisite card closes that).
- reattachAttempt compares attemptId, generation, processStartedAt and host as exact strings, and deliberately does NOT compare workerId or runnerId — claim opens attempts with runnerId = workerId, so comparing them would refuse every genuine reattach.
- moe.heartbeat's reattach answer carries reason, reattachWith, attemptId and phase, but NO generation, so the sidecar must hold the generation it pinned at claim time.
- Both sidecars today build one JSON-RPC request, pipe it through the proxy and discard the reply (sh: a background subshell using moe_rpc; ps1: a Start-Job script block piping into node). Both can capture and parse it with what they already have.
- Wave 1 acceptance case 4 passes only because its fixture writes the identity into the attempt record and plays the runner itself; it stays untouched here.
- The wrapper already reads its pinned attempt record from .moe/attempts/<id>.json in the finalize ladder, so the main-loop reattach needs no new read path.
planningNotes.risks:
1. Gated on task-bd799955: until the daemon records the identity, every arm here is vacuous. Step 1 verifies it in source, not just on the board.
2. Identity portability: /proc/$$/stat exists on Linux, WSL and Git Bash's MSYS but not macOS, where `ps -p $$ -o lstart=` is the fallback. Whitespace must be collapsed or the same process can spell it two ways.
3. A partial identity (one value resolved, the other not) is worse than none: it records something no reattach can reproduce. Send neither.
4. The sidecar is a separate process that outlives a careless wrapper exit; keep its stop paths exactly as they are.
5. MOE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SEC raised past reconcileWindowMs would let the window expire between pings. Call it out in the self-review; do not silently clamp it.
6. Both launchers or neither, and parity must stay green.
7. postflight.sh is about 36 minutes and the ps1 twin must be launched from PowerShell.
